title: Invocation state transitions are physical subtree moves between directories, not status flags
content:
For the repeatable Operational Primitives, the Artifact spells out the transition rule rather than leaving it implied. A.6.1.1.8.2.2.1.1.4: "Invocations that are completed successfully are moved to ... Active Instances Directory, whereas failed Invocations are Archived in ... Hub Data Repository." A.6.1.1.8.2.2.1.4 repeats it from the other side: "Once an Invocation is successfully completed, its subtree will be moved to ... Active Instances." The Light Agent Primitive carries identical language (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.3.1.4, A.6.1.1.8.2.2.3.4).

The design consequence is that a document's *position in the tree* is the state machine. There is no separate status field to disagree with the filing; being in Active Instances is what it means to be active.

This makes state changes auditable as document edits — a transition is a move recorded in the Artifact's own edit history, so it inherits the same review path as any other Artifact change. It also makes the failure path non-destructive: failed Invocations are archived rather than deleted, so the record of what was attempted and did not succeed survives.

The cost is that reading current state requires walking the tree, and two directories can never be updated atomically — a move is the only primitive available.
description: A successful Invocation's subtree moves from In Progress Invocations into Active Instances; a failed one is archived in the Hub Data Repository, so location is the authoritative state.
